THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, ALOK ARADHE J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Sri. D.L.N. Rao, learned Senior Counsel for Sri.Raghavendra Kattimani, learned counsel for the appellant.
Sri. B. Rajendra Prasad, learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Sri.K.N.Puttegowda, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Sri. T.P.Rajendra Kumar Sungay, learned counsel for respondent No.3.

This intra Court appeal has been filed against the order dated 23.08.2011 passed by the learned Single Judge by which the writ petition preferred by the appellant has been disposed of with a direction to the Bangalore Development Authority to consider and decide the representation dated 29.06.2011 submitted by the appellant.
2. The facts giving rise to filing of this appeal briefly stated are that the appellant is a Co-operative Society registered under the provisions of Karnataka Co- operative Societies Act, 1959.

The Society vide registered sale deed dated 17.05.1971 had purchased land measuring 34 guntas of Sy.No.254/1 M/S The Samuha Seva House Building ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148635457/
2 situated at Banasawadi Village, K.R.Puram Hobli, Bangalore East Taluk.

sentences.text: It appears that the Authority was in need of land held by the appellant and several other lands for formation of Old Madras-Banaswadi Road (OMBR) Scheme.
The preliminary notification under Section 17 of the BDA Act dated 03.11.1977 was issued.
Thereafter, a final notification under Section 19 of the BDA Act was issued on 13.11.1980.
3. It is pertinent to note that neither in the preliminary notification nor in the final notification, the name of the appellant was mentioned.

Thereafter on 26.12.1994, spot inspection was conducted and the spot inspection report was submitted by the Special Additional Land Acquisition Officer,
Bangalore Development Authority on 07.06.1995, in which it was found that the appellant is in possession of the land measuring 0.34 guntas of Sy.No.254/1.
4.
Thereafter, the Authority did not take any steps to conclude the proceedings for acquisition of land and passed the award after a period of 33 years on 10.07.2010.
In the aforesaid award also it was mentioned that the appellant is in possession of the land in question.

5. Thereupon, the appellant filed the writ petition seeking quashment of the preliminary as well as final notifications dated 03.11.1977 and 13.11.1980 respectively insofar as it related to the land held by the appellant.
Learned Single Judge however by an order dated 23.08.2011 directed the Authority to consider the representation dated 29.06.2011 submitted by the appellant.
In the aforesaid factual background, this appeal has been filed.
6. Learned Senior Counsel for the appellant submitted that no notice of land acquisition proceedings was ever given to the appellant.
It is further submitted that on 26.12.1994, spot inspection was conducted, in which the appellant was found to be in possession of the land.
It is also urged that till today, the appellant continues to be in possession of the land and no compensation has been paid to him.

It is also urged that possession of adjoining land which was held by the Hindustan Steel Rolling Mills has also been taken by the appellant, which shows that Authority has abandoned the acquisition proceedings.

In support of the aforesaid submission, a reliance has been placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'GRANULES INDIA LIMITED VS. UNION OF INDIA', 2020 SCC Online SC 71 as well as the judgment dated 28.02.2022 of the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.26920/2010 (CHIKKATHAYAPPA REDDY AND OTHERS VS.
STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER).
7.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Authority has submitted that the writ petition suffers from the delay and latches and the appellant is not entitled to any relief.
8. We have considered the submissions made on both sides and have perused the records.

9. The right to hold the property is a constitutional right which is guaranteed under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India and no citizen can be deprived of his property without following the due process of law.

It is well settled legal proposition that where a statute does not provide for time limit for doing an Act, such an Act has to be done within a reasonable time, and what would be reasonable time has to be decided in the facts and circumstances of the Act.
[See:'MEHER RUSI DALAL V M/S The Samuha Seva House Building ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 February, 2023

sentences.text: 10. Thus from the aforesaid well settled legal position, it is evident that the proceedings under the Act have to be concluded within a reasonable time.
11. In the light of the well settled legal principles, we may advert to the facts in hand.
In the instant case, preliminary notification was issued on 03.11.1977 and final notification was issued on 13.11.1980.
After a period of 33 years, an award was passed on 10.07.2010.
Thus, there has been inordinate delay in passing the award and the proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act has not been concluded within a reasonable time.
The award insofar as it pertains to land in question held by the appellant cannot be sustained in the eye of law.
12. For yet another reason, the land acquisition proceeding in respect of the land in question cannot be sustained.
It is pertinent to note that admittedly, the authority did not give any notice of land acquisition to the appellant.

The appellant has not been afforded an opportunity to file an objection to the land acquisition proceedings, neither any compensation has been paid to the appellant nor the possession of the land in question has been taken.
13. The fact that the appellant continues to be in possession of the land is axiomatic from the spot inspection conducted on 07.06.1995 as well as award which has been passed on 13.11.1980.
It is also pertinent to mention that in the spot inspection report it has been stated that the land in question is not suitable for formation of layout.
14. For the aforementioned reasons, the land acquisition proceedings insofar as it pertains to the land held by the appellant are vitiated in law and same cannot be sustained.
The order dated 23.08.2011 passed by the learned Single Judge is hereby set aside.
The preliminary as well as final notifications dated 03.11.1977 and 13.11.1980 as well as award dated 10.07.2010 insofar as it pertains to land held by the appellant is hereby quashed.
In the result, writ appeal is allowed.
